reference_25.citation: Zhou J, Liu Y, Ma J, et al. Prevalence of depressive symptoms among children and adolescents in China: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Child Adolesc Psychiatry Ment Health. 2024;18:150.
reference_25.design: Systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis; eligible ages 6-24; searches in PubMed, EMBASE, CNKI, WANFANG through 2024-10-15; publication years 1988-2024; no unified fieldwork period reported.
reference_25.evidence_type: Peer-reviewed journal review/meta-analysis; not primary intervention evidence.

checked_results.overall: 439 studies; 1,497,524 participants; pooled depressive-symptom screening positive proportion 26.17% (95% CI 25.00-27.41); I2=100%; p<0.001.
checked_results.cutoffs: Eight instruments used; authors did not subgroup the same instrument by different cutoffs.
checked_results.publication_bias: Funnel asymmetry and Egger z=-9.17, p<0.01 reported.
checked_results.quality_reporting: Authors report quality scores 3-8, median 6; 8/439 described nonresponders clearly; 141/439 lacked confidence intervals or subgroup details.

limits_for_claims: Screen-positive depressive symptoms are not a clinical diagnosis or local prevalence estimate.
I2=100%, varying instruments/cutoffs and publication bias materially limit transferability.
Stage subgroup k and n are not mutually exclusive; stage differences are descriptive and do not establish causes.
The high-school minus primary-school point estimate difference of 11.26 percentage points is descriptive only, not a pairwise test.
reference_25.correction_retraction_check: No correction/retraction notice surfaced in publisher-page and exact-title/DOI web checks performed 2026-10-27; not an exhaustive registry/Crossmark search.

observations: The supplement lists 33 rows including Hong Kong, Taiwan, and Tianjin; proposal charts 31 mainland rows.
The paper states its map excludes Macau and 29 articles with unspecified or multi-province sites.
Tianjin estimate derives from a multisite study; it is not a Tianjin-only study.
Abstract wording assigns Qinghai/Tibet study counts in an order that conflicts with Supplementary Table S2; frozen data follows the detailed table and notes the discrepancy.
Regional subgroup estimates are not representative province-level population rates.

new_ai_sources.checked_claim: Describes combining parametric language-model memory with nonparametric retrieved passages; evaluations are general knowledge-intensive NLP tasks, not mental-health service studies.

correction.scope: Publisher correction states references 1-14 were disordered in initial version due to a conversion error; HTML/PDF references corrected.

new_ai_sources.citation: Guo Z, Lai A, Thygesen JH, et al. Large Language Models for Mental Health Applications: Systematic Review. JMIR Ment Health. 2024;11:e57400.
new_ai_sources.checked_claim: PRISMA review searched through 2024-04-30 and evaluated 40 articles across detection, conversational-agent and other mental-health tasks; reports risks including inconsistent outputs, hallucinations, limited ethical benchmarks and need for professional oversight. Review findings are heterogeneous and not direct evidence for this platform.

workflow: Deterministic code calculates confirmed fields, missingness and comparable same-version scores.
RAG retrieves only approved institutional information and returns document/version/paragraph provenance.
LLM drafts a four-part summary: recorded facts, cited information, missing information, and questions for human confirmation.
Assigned professional checks source records, edits or discards draft and remains responsible for communication/action.
prohibited_claims_without_new_validation: AI accurately diagnoses depression or determines crisis level.
AI reduces workload, improves mental health, or improves referral outcomes.
Current prototype has validated model performance.

reproducibility_difficulty.deterministic_statistics: low, after the instrument, data dictionary and score conventions have been confirmed
reproducibility_difficulty.controlled_RAG: moderate; requires a frozen corpus/index/retrieval configuration and human relevance labels
reproducibility_difficulty.LLM_summary_evaluation: moderate-high; requires fixed synthetic cases, exact model/version, prompts, sampling settings, rubric and blinded dual review; hosted model drift can impede exact repeatability
reproducibility_difficulty.clinical_or_service_outcomes: high; requires school and ethics approval, expert staff, real-world protocol, sampling, monitoring and safety stop rules

ai_integration.recommended_proposal_paragraph: Project AI is limited to reviewed-information retrieval and draft organization. Deterministic code first processes records against an approved field dictionary and instrument version, marking missing or incomparable items. Retrieval returns source passages from approved institutional materials with version and location. A language model drafts a four-part summary of recorded facts, source material, missing information and questions for staff to confirm. Staff compare the draft with original records, edit or discard it, and remain responsible for communication and decisions. The first evaluation will use fixed synthetic cases to assess factual support, omissions, citations, boundary violations, staff edits and failure fallback. Further evaluation is contingent on school approval, role assignment, data governance and professional review.
